### Observed differences

- In the later window, A02 takes part in about 65 in 100 cases (130 of 200) versus about 21 in 100 before (41 of 200), and its mean occurrences per trace rise from about 0.22 to about 0.70. [OCC001]
- A02's position within cases concentrates at the end: before, it appeared at widely varying positions (median about two-thirds into the case, a quarter of occurrences in the first fifth); in the later window the median is about 0.97 of the case length and almost all occurrences sit in the last few events. [POS001]
- A02's observed outgoing transitions now go to A46 in about 92 in 100 cases (about 30 in 100 before), while its former targets A15 (about 19 in 100), A16 (about 12) and A20 (about 7) are no longer observed; A02 is followed by A46 within one step in about 99 in 100 of the observed pairs (about 74 in 100 before, on only 16 pairs). [DIR001, LAG002]
- A02 now co-occurs with A14, A15, A29, A30, A45 and A46 in about 65 in 100 cases each (about 10–21 in 100 before) and typically follows them: A14 first in about 60 in 100 cases (18 before), A29 in about 60 (10), A30 in about 59 (9), A45 in about 60 (6); A02 precedes A46 in about 61 in 100 cases (19 before). [REL001, REL002, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- A45's outgoing transitions now go to A02 in about 63 in 100 cases (about 6 in 100 before), and A45→A46 shifted from one step apart (about 85 in 100) to two steps apart (about 64 in 100), matching A02 now sitting between them. [DIR011, LAG012, LAG013]
- Routing among A21, A22, A23, A24, A29 and A30 changed from a mixed pattern to a fixed sequence: A23 and A24 now lead to A30 in about 94–97 in 100 of their outgoing transitions (about 48–51 before), A21 and A22 now lead mainly to A24 (about 52–56) and A23 (about 40–44) and almost never directly to A30 (about 1–2, versus 45–51 before), and A29 now leads almost only to A21 and A22 (about 97 in 100 combined, versus a spread over four targets before). [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, REL011]
- The lags agree with that sequence: A21→A30 and A22→A30 now occur two steps apart (about 95–97 in 100) rather than one, A23→A30, A24→A30, A29→A21 and A29→A22 occur one step apart (about 95–99), and A29→A23/A24 two steps apart. [LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011]
- A06 takes part in about 7 in 100 cases in the later window (13 of 200) versus about 21 in 100 before (41 of 200); its later routing profile rests on only 13 traces and is not interpretable in detail. [OCC002, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, A02 is executed as a standard late step in the case — after A14/A15 and the A29/A30/A45 stage, and immediately before A46 — in about two in three cases, whereas before it ran in about one in five cases at scattered positions. In the same window, the A21–A24 block, which previously routed mixedly to A30 and among itself, now runs in a fixed order A29 → A21/A22 → A23/A24 → A30, and A06 is executed in far fewer cases. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR011, OCC002, REL001, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, LAG002, LAG013]

The placement hypothesis rests on direct relational and positional evidence, not only on frequency: A02's participation roughly tripled while its position concentrated at the end of the case, the relation items show A02 following A14/A15/A29/A30/A45 and preceding A46, and the direction and lag items show the A45→A02→A46 sequence directly. The chain change is likewise shown by successor shares and lags that agree. Counting the A02 repositioning, the A21–A30 chain and the A06 drop as three distinct differences, this clearly exceeds the roughly 0.7 items expected by chance among the 141 tested units, and each difference is larger than what random re-splits of the pooled traces produced in all but about 1 in 200 reference comparisons. [OCC001, POS001, REL009, REL010, DIR011, LAG012, LAG013, DIR005, LAG003, LAG005, OCC002]

Limitations: the two windows are finite samples, so the evidence cannot rule out that the later window simply contains a larger share of a variant that includes a late A02 and the sequential A21–A30 chain, without a change to the shared structure; it also cannot distinguish A02 having been repositioned from early A02 occurrences disappearing while late ones became standard. Some profiles are thinly supported — A06's later routing rests on 13 traces and one lag item (A24→A21) on a single observation — so beyond its frequency drop, A06's later behaviour remains uncertain. [OCC002, DIR002, LAG006, POS001]
